[quote=new_westmore;61542928]The elder starts shouting at Ahmed. "What are you doing, you absolute rube?! You're going to expose us!" The elder tries to stop Ahmed from throwing more boxes out of the airplane, pinning the distressed man to a seat by his neck.

"Grant, get this thing down on the ground NOW!"

Grant grunts. "Yeah, I'm working on that. Don't let Ahmed throw more stuff out, mate, he'll knock our center of gravity off!"

...

Down on the ground, reports of boxes falling and smacking down on cars and other assorted things deluges the local police of Edmundsen. Some of the boxes have spilled their contents all over the ground, revealing guns, exploded bags of drugs and more.

It is a harrowing sight to many, who have no idea what's going on.

...

Grant manages to line up the plane with the runway, and brings it in for a shaky landing. His mood drops even further, as he sees an assortment of red and blue lights all over the field.

"We've got a problem. A big one."[/quote]
Ahmed thrashes around trying to break free, but he is not a strong man, his body relaxes and he curses his rotten luck while Grant and the Elder handle whatever remains of the planes problems.

[b]On the Home Front[/b]

It had been only one day since the ceasefire had been declared, and the HDF continued its assault on Rosenmarkke, despite the ceasefire with Wuloosya. This time it seemed that they had begun to target the SCSIDs island intelligence plan. 

However, attacking the islands had always been considered by the SCSID a highly suicidal move by any nation, this had been proven in the 1961 lake of pigs invasion by Vespurias, the 1932 bombing by Montfleur, the 1917 bombing by Llyndora, and the 1870 attempted invasion by Montfleur. 

Firstly the islands were intentionally prepared for guerilla style warfare, secondly they were within range of both Vespurian and Rosenmarkket mainland SAM systems and had SAM systems on the islands themselves.

Of the first wave of attacks, consisting of drones, FAMM missiles, cruise missiles, and Tomahwak missiles, initial strikes would hit various targets across major docks in Rosenmarkke, killing civilians who had unfortunately been working in the docks or were nearby the docks as further fuel and other equipment burst into flames. The damage would be immense, as smoke drifted into the night sky across several Rosenmarkket ports. The SAM systems would shoot down further volleys after the initial strikes, but with radar blinking on and of course damages done to the coastal radar stations, there would be minor faults in the defense, which were in the process of getting fixed but hadnt yet been fixed.

As bombs continued to rain down, with the artillery positions and bunkers now being targeted, the armed forces would order all artillery on the island to be moved immediately into caves and undercroppings, with the islands, being made of large chalk and limestone caves allowing for immediate repositioning. Although damage would be sustained with 203 howitzers sustaining damage, and 140 soldiers being injured due to the explosions, villagers and reservists would begin establishing gun firing lines at the drones, with the SCSID working quickly to cut off their GPS and internet connections potential making them inoperable. Hackers on the mainland, familiar with AI systems thanks to the THEP integrated AI program that had begun earlier in the year would move to disrupt the machine learning mechanisms through the use of jamming and disruptive code.

As energy and defense nodes were targeted, power to various towns and half of the nations largest city would be disrupted, shutting off systems in hospitals and other civilian infrastructure in the region. These would be quickly put back up by local systems, however, damage had been done to the power lines leading to three of the major naval-air bases along the strait, forcing them into their secondary power nodes. 

The thermobaric bombs would hit their targets, although some SAM systems would manage to shoot them down and blow them up mid-air, although various would hit their targets, leading to widespread fires.

The battle now turned to the sea, with LRSAM missiles being fired from B1-B Lancer Bombers at supply and transport ships, however, Rosenmarkke wasnt stupid enough to transport its weapons or its troops on openly marked military ships, though several had been sent into the strait. 

As these few that had been sent into the strait were predictably struck, the SCSID would order all convoys to avoid traditional convoy flows, utilising smaller deliveries and undesignated or unmarked ships to travel to randomised pick-up spots. No civilians would be injured during these operations, however, 12 cargo ships with military equipment would be crippled with 2 later sinking with a loss of 70% of the equipment onboard one and 30% onboard the other. 

As the HDF attempted to strike the rest of the Rosenmarkket fleet, assuming and probably seeing that 10 ships had been sunk, the SCSID would send up further false signatures, radar, moving reserve ships into the open waters as decoys. 

To counter the submarine warfare, the submarines already in the sea would be ordered into complete radar and operational silence, utlising the natural seafloor and coastline to hide into them, with above water anti-UUV efforts being made by both fishermen, and the SCSID, utilising hacking and jamming to confuse the UUVs. Utilising the non-deployed Akira Class submarines, the Rosenmarkket navy would begin hunting the SSGNs, taking advantage of the classs speed and agility.

Unfortunately two diesel electric submarines would be lost in the effort. Killing 100 sailors.

Rosenmarkke would issue an order to close the landward side of the strait from all international naval traffic, due to the wide operating range of the HDF. 

As the air battle began, the SCSID adopted a quickfire plan, consisting of disrupting the CCAs using passive hunting tactics and long range shots at them by the F-35s, utilising their stealth capabilities to do so. Furthermore an interceptor screen consisting of Mig-29s in the front, Su-30s and Rafaels into the back, in order to force an earlier and closer fight with the HDF fighters. Datalink, spoofing, and decoy aircraft signatures would further be used against the CCAs

In order to protect the tankers, they would be moved up to 600-700 km from the main front, beyond the range of the HDF fighters and bombers, with various smaller refeuling tracks being utilised. To address damage to oil and resupply done earlier by the initial volley of missiles during Operation Crusader, the SCSID would order emergency reserves to be loaded into mobile tanker trucks to disperse the oil refilling points away from major targets. 

Three AWAC craft would be lost unfortunately, with Rosenmarkke utilising ship, ground, and F-35 passive hunting to lower radar emissions.

To counter ALBMs the SCSID would order all secondary airfields readied, with air specialist crews in the regions being dispersed to them. Furthermore highways in marked areas would be cleared to provide for landing should the craft need to be landed, with tanker trucks being placed on standby within these regions to ensure quick turn over. 

In the meantime Rosenmarkke would move to target the J-15 launch craft, JA-35s, and JA-18 carriers using long range air to air strikes and stealth interceptions. 

In the meantime an order would be given out ordering all citizens with weapons to Fire at any low-flying drone regardless of its origins, with flights and all other air traffic being grounded. 

In the meantime the EDU had begun to hunt for the bunkers where the leadership had been hidden, with the decoy bunkers being mainly destroyed, the main bunkers were like white sheep in a field of black sheep, however, to minimise signatures the main government bunkers would use low-emitting energy generators, with a naturalised blinking pattern being established for energy. Air recycling would also be utilised within the bunkers, however unfortunately the bunkers located along the Montfleurois border and Rosenmarkket border would be destroyed by a bunker buster, killing 40 SCSID staffers and 3 commanders of the SCSID.

In a written statement the Council of 99 would declare:

[i]It has become evident that the presence of the HDF in this conflict has gone beyond the mandate of support and has breached into open war with Rosenmarkke, it is in this manner the council of 99 hereby demands that the Wuloosyan government call back its hounds, or Rosenmarkke shall call forward its own hounds.[/i]

[i]"I'm getting the f*ck out of here,"[/i] he screams. [i]"I ain't going to jail over this!"[/i]

Ahmed waits for the elder to get off of him, he makes his way to his cracked phone and tries calling his wife, whilst the phone rings, he cracks open the boxes with the phone pressed to his ear with assistance from his shoulder. He grabs a pistol and a grenade. 

[i]"Old man take what you will, then piss off, im chucking a grenade in this thing. They're not getting OUR sh!t, ya dig?"[/i]

The phone continues to ring.

The elder nods. He picks up a rifle from one of the boxes still on board, shoves some magazines into his clothes and runs out of the airplane. Outside, the cops are already beginning to close in on the airplane, sirens blaring and guns pointed at their men of the hour.

...

Grant runs across several taxiways as he desperately tries to put distance between him and the airplane. He doesn't care for where he's going; all he wants to do is get out.

Running in an airfield, especially an active one, is a surefire way to get yourself killed.

Grant looks back at the airplane in the distance. The cops have already surrounded it. Just as he turns around, he runs head on into the side of an airplane engine, knocking himself out cold.

The entire airport goes still. From the tower, a bright orange flash illuminates the faces of the controllers.

Looking on in horror, everyone can now see that the pathetic Metroliner that dropped its load over Edmundsen is now no more but a smouldering wreck in the middle of the runway. Amidst the flames, a shootout ensues, as Ahmed and the elder fight tooth and nail for their freedom. All they need to do is to reach the southern end of the field, and then they can escape.

On the ground, the elder hears a different siren. It sounds like the kind that they would blare in times of crisis. Looking behind him, he can see how that the air base's lights have turned on, and that pouring out through the doors are a mass of uniformed men holding service rifles of their own.

Is this the end for him?

He respects the old man for staying behind, and generally follows his lead, even if that lead is running out of the only shelter they have.

So this is how God has decided to punish him?

He throws the rifle down and falls to his knees, defeated. The airmen surround him and force him down to the ground, promptly arresting him for his misdeeds against the good people of the nation.
